text:
HSTU already has a strong multi-negative precedent: Meta’s released 2024 configuration uses sampled softmax with 128 uniformly sampled negatives, L2-normalized embeddings and temperature 0.05. This supports an objective-only experiment while preserving the corrected HSTU backbone; those settings are starting points, not evidence of optimality for these Amazon categories. [Official configuration](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/configs/ml-1m/hstu-sampled-softmax-n128-final.gin). The 2024 gSASRec extended abstract offers a competing hypothesis: multiple negatives plus generalized BCE reduce sampling-induced overconfidence. Its loss can be tested within HSTU without adopting the SASRec architecture. [Paper](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf).

Sampling correction and false-negative handling address different problems. The 2025 “Correcting the LogQ Correction” paper identifies popularity bias from in-batch negatives and treats the always-present positive separately in its correction; avoid applying an assumed popularity correction to uniform sampling. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331). False-negative mitigation should first exclude the target, padding and known training-history positives, using no held-out interactions. A 2026 sequential-recommendation paper studies semantic negative filtering, but its diffusion and category/brand components exceed this objective-only experiment and the available metadata. [Paper](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950705126010221).

Suggested bounded comparison: existing BCE versus sampled softmax with 32/128 negatives, then multi-negative gBCE; keep one HSTU checkpoint per category. These are experimental proposals, not established improvements. A 2026 preprint cautions that more negatives can underperform larger batches under fixed memory, so measure training cost alongside pinned macro validation HR@10. Preserve seeds, routing, splits and training caps; use no test metrics. [Budget study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11061).
